newsitem.title: SWEDEN: More steps possible to cut Swedish jobless-Fin Min.
newsitem.headline: More steps possible to cut Swedish jobless-Fin Min.

text.p: More measures to tackle Swedish unemployment could be introduced in the autumn budget to help the government reach its goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000, Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday.
"It is not impossible," Asbrink told reporters after a Social Democrat economic seminar when asked if the budget would include more measures.
The finance minister did not want to discuss details but emphasised that economic policies must be designed to increase employment.
"It is obvious. We have three years, and it would be surprising if we did not do more in this period," Asbrink said.
He said the best way to tackle unemployment was through sound state finances and low inflation. He played down the significance of structural changes in the labour market.
"There is a tendency for people to over-emphasise the signficance (of structural reforms)," Asbrink said.
